hook: A graph is a picture of how one quantity depends on another, and two features of it carry most of the physics: how steep it is and how much area sits under it. Read those two and you can get a speed, a distance or an acceleration without a single equation.

prereq.q: A walker covers 12 m in 6.0 s at a steady speed. What is her speed?
prereq.why: Speed = distance ÷ time = 12 m ÷ 6.0 s = 2.0 m/s.

prereq.q: If y ∝ x², what happens to y when x triples?
options: It becomes one ninth as large

figure.caption: The slope is rise over run, in (y unit)/(x unit). The area under a line is height × width, in (y unit) × (x unit).

chain.cause: A graph has a quantity with a unit on each axis
chain.effect: its slope and its area each have a unit, built from those two units

chain.cause: You divide the rise by the run between two points on a line
chain.effect: you get the slope, the rate at which y changes per unit of x

chain.cause: You multiply the height by the width of the region under a graph
chain.effect: you get an area whose unit is (y unit) × (x unit), often a total such as a distance

chain.cause: Data scatter and the relationship may be curved
chain.effect: you draw a best-fit line, after choosing what to plot so the graph is straight

ideas: Every axis gets a label and a unit: "Time (s)". Without both, the graph cannot be read.
Slope = rise/run = Δy/Δx, from two points on the line (not data points). Its unit is (y unit)/(x unit), and it is a rate.
Area under a graph = height × width for a rectangle, ½ × base × height for a triangle. Its unit is (y unit) × (x unit).
A best-fit line passes between scattered points, never dot to dot. If the relationship is curved, linearize: for d = ½at², plot d against t², and the slope is ½a.

misconception.wrong: To find a slope, divide the y-value of a point by its x-value, for example 9.0 m ÷ 10 s for a line through (0 s, 2.0 m) and (10 s, 9.0 m).
misconception.right: A slope uses changes between two points on the line: (9.0 m − 2.0 m) ÷ (10 s − 0 s) = 0.70 m/s. Dividing one point's values works only when the line passes through the origin.

summary: Label every axis with a quantity and unit. The slope of a line is Δy/Δx between two points on it, with units (y unit)/(x unit); the area under a graph is height × width, with units (y unit) × (x unit). Fit a line to data, and linearize a curved relationship before fitting.
